blocks.text: With Leo Reich, Emily Fairn, Olive Gray

Ethan, Abi and Sam, inseparable friends in their mid-20s, are forced into real adulthood when eviction looms. Razor-sharp and witty, It Gets Worse skewers a generation stuck between housing crisis, humiliating jobs and messy relationships, while savouring the joy of youth in one of the buzziest cities in the world. It’s anchored by standout performances from the three leads, alongside unforgettable cameos from the likes of Lena Dunham and Andrew Scott.
Contains scenes of drug use, nudity, and sex.
Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .
For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.
If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.
More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

blocks.text: A jaded New York club promoter finds his messy lifestyle upended by the discovery that he has a son, in Jordan Firstman’s hilarious feature directorial debut.
I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning

In Clio Barnard’s poignant drama, five childhood friends from Birmingham find their lifelong bonds tested as adulthood brings fractured relationships, unfulfilled dreams and long-buried secrets to light.
The Trip to the Northern Lights
Rob Brydon and Steve Coogan are back on the road, sharing delicious meals, hilarious banter and celebrity impressions as they journey through northern Europe.
